name: Tunnel mouth (SS)
description:
Shape Survivors set dressing: a hole dug up through the field from below, and the same hole caved in. The spoil is heaped highest on the near lip where it was pushed out, and it is warm turned earth rather than the ruins' purple stone — the one ring on this ground that means dug, not built. Drawn at the crater tilt the pheromone vent uses, so a mouth cut into open flats and one cut into a burrow chamber read as the same object.

The rim is built in banded slopes rather than as one flat ellipse, and every band takes its side from one light, up-screen: the far bank's crest is lit (`bank_lit`) and the near bank's outer slope falls into shadow (`bank_shade`); inside the lip that reverses, because the wall you can see into a tilted hole is the far one and it faces away from the light (`wall_shade`), while the near lip's crest catches it on the turn as a thin bright line (`rim_lit`). `lip_edge` is the hard ink line the ground breaks on, drawn over the throat so the hole keeps its edge however far the thing inside it opens.

Everything inside the mouth is its own part, because a track can name one part and only one: the throat, the dark it pools into, the four rings of muscle down it, and each of the fourteen teeth set into the lip. A tooth is one husk polygon with an ink stroke, and its origin is its root on the lip rather than the middle of the hole, so what a track moves is a tooth hinged where a tooth is attached. The ring is laid out on the un-tilted circle the mouth is a projection of and projected with it, so the foreshortening is the hole's own: the pair at the sides stand at full length while the ones on the near and far lips are seen nearly end-on.

**The drawing is the mouth open, and the mouth is shut for nearly all of its life.** `idle` is it clamped: every tooth driven inward along its own radius until the ring meets in the middle, grown a fifth longer on the way so what closes the hole is teeth crossing rather than a ring shrinking, sunk into the hole and dimmed towards the ink under them; the throat constricted behind them and gone dark, the folds squeezed shut. `open` unclenches it, `sense` holds it that way, `shut` closes it again.

There is no bite clip. A tunnel spends itself the instant somebody drops through and the caved-in plug goes in on the spot, so the closing that used to be the swallow is now simply `shut` — which means the player is shown the bite every time they walk away from a mouth instead of once, on the one frame they were busy falling. The teeth are still the only warning the object gives, and now the warning is a thing you watch happen twice.

Both one-shots are generated as interpolations between the exact first frames of the loops either side of them, and every wobble in `idle` is zero at t=0, so nothing in here is a pose written down twice and no handover can pop.

The `filled` variant is what a spent tunnel leaves: the heap gone back down the hole, domed and paler than the ground it came out of, broken into clods on top and sunk away from the lip where it settled.

filled.description: Spent: the tunnel caved in. What blocks it is not a lid over the hole and not one lump either — it is a heap of loose spoil packed right out to the lip and piled past it, seven courses of clods narrowing as they climb, the big ones bedded in the crater and small pale pieces perched on the crest. A course is one seeded scatter drawn three times at that seed, so every clod carries its own rim, body and crown for three parts rather than thirty; each course is sparse enough to keep those rims, stepped far enough apart in y that it cannot climb over the one behind and bury it, and drawn over that one so its rims cut into it — which is what stacks them instead of laying them side by side. Angular rather than round, because earth breaks and does not bubble. The ring survives into this state on purpose: the digging happened, and filling it in does not put the ground back. The throat, its folds, the dark at the bottom of it, all fourteen teeth and the three inner rim bands go with it — a caved-in mouth cannot take anything from anybody, and any of that left standing over a plug would say it still could. The banked rim stays, because the digging happened and filling it in does not put the ground back. It is a still: `animations: []`, because nothing in a plug breathes.

idle.description:
Shut, and this is what a tunnel looks like for nearly all of a run. Every tooth has driven inward along its own radius until the ring meets in the middle and grown a fifth longer on the way, so the hole is closed by teeth crossing each other rather than by a ring that got smaller — each one still outlined against its neighbours by its own ink stroke. They are sunk into the hole and dimmed two thirds of the way towards the ink they lie over, because a jaw held shut is a jaw in its own shadow, and behind them the throat is constricted, dropped and gone dark with its folds squeezed almost out of sight.

It presses rather than breathes. A tooth already meshed with its neighbours bears down a fraction further and eases off, a fourteenth of a loop behind the one before it, and the whole ring turns very slightly with it — so a mouth across the field is a shut dark thing in a ring of fresh earth, and a mouth you are standing over is working on something.

open.description:
It unclenches. One shot, four tenths of a second, played the moment somebody comes inside `TUNNEL_SENSE_R` — and it is the whole warning the object gives, so it is built to be caught from the corner of an eye: the teeth withdraw along their own radii back out to the rim and shorten to their proper length, brightening as they come out of the hole's shadow; the throat rises, dilates and lights; the dark at the bottom recedes down it.

Two things make it a movement rather than a number going up. The hole throws itself a fifth wider than it will settle and comes back, and the teeth do not all let go together — each takes its own fraction of a frame, the near lip last, which is the clamp's own stagger run backwards.

Both ends are generated: the first frame is `idle` at t=0 and the last is `sense` at t=0, so this can be handed over on either side without a cut.

sense.description:
Held open, waiting. The hole is at full width, the teeth stand at full length out at the rim, the throat is dilated and its folds pulse twice a loop, and the teeth chatter — every other one turning against its neighbours, a motion no other state has and the one that says the mouth is working rather than sitting there. The ripple around the ring runs at twice the breath's rate over the top of that chatter, so no two teeth are ever in the same place.

It loops for as long as whatever tripped it stays near, which is the *waiting*: the thing is open and it is not doing anything else, and the next move is the player's.

shut.description:
The bite, and the only one this document has. It closes on whoever just walked away, which is the point — the swallow used to happen on the one frame the player was busy falling through, and now the same movement is shown every time somebody comes near a mouth and thinks better of it.

Each tooth drives inward along its own radius and grows as it goes, so the ring does not shrink — it closes. That distinction is the whole of it: teeth that scale down towards the middle leave a widening band of nothing between themselves and the lip and read as the mouth receding, where teeth that keep their size and cross each other read as a mouth shutting on something. They do not arrive together — each carries its own fraction of a frame of lateness and its own turn, some one way and some the other, and the near lip is a hair behind the far one, because a mouth shuts from the back of the throat out — and they overshoot the clamp and settle back onto it rather than stopping dead on it.

The throat goes with them and goes dark: the folds constrict fold by fold and fade as they do, the throat's own colour drops back towards the ink lip it is drawn over, and the dark at the bottom comes up to meet the teeth. What does not move is the edge — `lip_edge` and `wall_shade` hold their place, because the hole is still a hole in the ground however far shut the thing in it is.

Its last frame is `idle` at t=0.
